title: Decode Qwen3 4B faster
summary: Submit a decode engine for the pinned Qwen3 4B checkpoint; the judge times it against native Qwen on H100 and checks every token.
descriptionMd:
Decode Qwen3 4B faster on one NVIDIA H100.

Submit an inference engine for the pinned `Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507`
checkpoint, BF16 weights. Your `engine.py` exports `class Engine` with
`__init__(self, model_path)` and `generate(self, input_ids, max_new_tokens)`,
which yields one list with a token id per sequence for every output step,
exactly `max_new_tokens` times, without stopping at end-of-sequence tokens. The
engine owns the whole generation loop. The judge owns the prompts, the clock,
the native reference and the rule that every token must be what native Qwen
would produce under greedy decoding.

Nine workloads, each a fixed batch, prompt length and output length: three
public, shown below, and six private, which decide the score. For each, the
judge starts your engine in a fresh process, lets it load and warm up, then
times its samples from a separate trusted process that writes the prompt ids
to your engine and reads the token stream back. Native Qwen is timed by the
same clock through the same pipe for latency checks. Ranking uses output tokens
per second: batch size times output length divided by median generation seconds.
The leaderboard takes the geometric mean across the six private workloads,
with equal weight for each. Higher throughput wins. Public runs measure the
public workloads once each and never rank.

Your tokens are replayed through native Qwen, teacher-forced on your own
prefix. Each must be the argmax of the native logits at that position, or
within 2 logits of it: the margin absorbs BF16 near ties, not
approximations. A workload also fails, and with it the run, on time to first
token or time per output token above 1.10 times native (official runs), peak
GPU memory above 90% of the device, more than 25% spread across samples, or
an engine that fails to load within 300 seconds, crashes, emits the wrong
number of steps or tokens, or exceeds 300 seconds on one sample.

The runtime is the platform's: Python 3.11, CUDA 12.4, PyTorch 2.5.1, Triton
3.1.0, Transformers 4.51.3, no network. Vendor any Python or Triton source in
the archive (2 MiB compressed, 200 files); do not include weights,
credentials, compiled binaries or Docker images. Your engine runs as an
unprivileged process inside the timing container with read-only access to
the checkpoint. See docs/QWEN_ENGINE_CONTRACT.md for the full rules.
callable: Engine(model_path).generate(input_ids, max_new_tokens) -> iterator of per-step token lists
returns: greedy token stream; every token native Qwen's argmax or a near tie
